summary: Local ticket tracker: JSON tickets in status folders as an alternative to Jira
description:
Source: team sync 2026-11-04. The team has no Jira (or not ours), and the demo must run without it.

**Design:** a tracker interface with two backends, Jira (today) and local.

* **Local backend:** a folder per status (`todo/`, `in-progress/`, `done/`). One JSON file per ticket, same schema as `backlog/` (key, summary, description, acceptance criteria, labels, comments). Status is the folder; a transition moves the file.
* **Intake:** polls `todo/` for tickets labelled `anvil`.
* **Agent tools:** `jira_get`, `jira_comment`, `jira_transition`, `jira_create` and `jira_search` route to the configured backend. Names stay the same (or get neutral `ticket_*` aliases) so skills don't change.
* The approval gate on create stays.

**Acceptance:**

* dropping a TC1 ticket JSON into `todo/` starts a run;
* the run's comment lands in the file;
* the file ends in `in-progress/` or `done/`;
* with Jira credentials unset, nothing tries to reach Atlassian.

comments.body: [devin] PR #72 up: https://github.com/vishal7pandey/anvil/pull/72 — LocalTracker (ANVIL_TICKETS_DIR, todo/in-progress/done JSON files, backlog schema); intake polls it alongside Jira, Jira only when ATLASSIAN_* set; local runs get trigger local:<key>, path verbatim in Run.repo, offline network; jira_* tools bind to the store for local runs, no GitHub tools. Interface note for ANVIL-55: repo_path() must basename a local path. 6 new tests + 50 regression green.
